entries.title: II Corinthians 11:1
segments: I could wish that you would tolerate a little folly in me! But indeed you do tolerate me.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:2
segments: I am jealous over you with the jealousy of God. For I betrothed you to one husband, that I might present you to the Christ a pure bride.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:3
segments: Yet I fear that it may turn out that, just as the Serpent by his craftiness deceived Eve, so your minds may have lost the loyalty and purity due from you to the Christ.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:4
segments: For, if some new-comer is proclaiming a Jesus other than him whom we proclaimed, or if you are receiving a Spirit different from the Spirit which you received, or a Good News different from that which you welcomed, then you are marvelously tolerant!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:5
segments: I do not regard myself as in any way inferior to the most eminent Apostles!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:6
segments: Though I am no trained orator, yet I am not without knowledge; indeed we made this perfectly clear to you in every way.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:7
segments: Perhaps you say that I did wrong in humbling myself that you might be exalted--I mean because I told you God's Good News without payment.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:8
segments: I robbed other churches by taking pay from them, so that I might serve you!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:9
segments: And, when I was with you in need, I did not become a burden to any of you; for our Brothers, on coming from Macedonia, supplied my needs. I kept myself, and will keep myself from being an expense to you in any way.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:10
segments: As surely as I know anything of the Truth of Christ, this boast, as far as I am concerned, shall not be stopped in any part of Greece.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:11
segments: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows that I do!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:12
segments: What I am doing now I shall continue to do, that I may cut away the ground from under those who are wishing for some ground for attacking me, so that as regards the thing of which they boast they may appear in their true characters, just as we do.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:13
segments: Men of this stamp are false apostles, treacherous workers, disguising themselves as Apostles of Christ!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:14
segments: And no wonder; for even Satan disguises himself as an angel of Light.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:15
segments: It is not surprising, therefore, if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of Righteousness. But their end will be in accordance with their actions.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:16
segments: I say again--Let no one think me a fool! Yet, if you do, at least welcome me as you would a fool, that I, too may indulge in a little boasting.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:17
segments: When I speak thus, I am not speaking as the Master would, but as a fool might, in boasting so confidently.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:18
segments: As so many are boasting of earthly things, I, too, will boast.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:19
segments: For all your cleverness, you tolerate fools willingly enough!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:20
segments: You tolerate a man even when he enslaves you, when he plunders you, when he gets you into his power, when he puts on airs of superiority, when he strikes you in the face!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:21
segments: I admit, to my shame, that we have been weak. But whatever the subject on which others are not afraid to boast--though it is foolish to say so--I am not afraid either!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:22
segments: Are they Hebrews? So am I! Are they Israelites? So am I! Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:23
segments: Are they 'Servants of Christ'? Though it is madness to talk like this, I am more so than they! I have had more of toil, more of imprisonment! I have been flogged times without number. I have been often at death's door.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:24
segments: Five times I received at the hands of the Jews forty lashes, all but one.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:25
segments: Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was shipwrecked. I have spent a whole day and night in the deep.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:26
segments: My journeys have been many. I have been through dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from my own people, dangers from the Gentiles, dangers in towns, dangers in the country, dangers on the sea, dangers among false Brothers.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:27
segments: I have been through toil and hardship. I have passed many a sleepless night; I have endured hunger and thirst; I have often been without food; I have known cold and nakedness.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:28
segments: And, not to speak of other things, there is my daily burden of anxiety about all the Churches.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:29
segments: Who is weak without my being weak? Who is led astray without my burning with indignation?

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:30
segments: If I must boast, I will boast of things which show my weakness!

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:31
segments: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus--he who is for ever blessed--knows that I am speaking the truth.

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:32
segments: When I was in Damascus, the Governor under King Aretas had the gates of that city guarded, so as to arrest me,

entries.title: II Corinthians 11:33
segments: But I was let down in a basket through a window in the wall, and so escaped his hands.
